prudence.title: Cassiere
prudence.bio: Has counted the same chest twice daily for thirty-one years and found it short only once, which he still mentions.

thin_till: If three depositors come at once, we shut the bench. Remember the one that broke at Easter.
Writing in a book does not pay the widow who asks for her coin.
flush_till: Idle coin never yet broke a bench.
Let the chest be heavy. Heavy chests sleep well, and so do I.
high_leverage: Three ducats written for every one in the chest. The Senate has banished bankers for less.
Book money is a promise. Promises do not clink.
big_prince_exposure: The Commune pays when it pleases, and it is rarely pleased.
Every forced loan is a coin I shall never count again.
bubble_city: When the fishwife borrows to buy pepper, sell the pepper.
Half the Rialto is borrowing on the same cargo. One storm, sers.
far_branches: Our man in Bruges could be dead a month and still signing letters.
Distance is where honest factors become rich ones.
loss_turn: I said so. Write it in the book, and write it plainly.
Draw in the loans before the depositors draw out their coin.
good_turn: Good. Put the profit in the chest, not on a galley.
A profit is a pleasant thing. A reserve is a useful one.
court_offer: The Doge asks; the Doge does not repay. Lend a little, gracefully.
Ask for a pledge. Salt, jewels, anything I can weigh.
new_tech: New ways of writing are new ways of hiding.
Forty years in Roman numerals and the book balances. Why change?
centre_moving: Let the money wander. Venice will be here when it returns.
Bruges? They pay in cloth and excuses.
quiet: Quiet is my favourite season.
Count the chest. Then count it again.

court.name: Ser Andrea Querinetto
court.title: Agent to the Signoria
court.bio: Knows which Procurator dines where, which Senator owes whom, and pretends to know nothing of either.

thin_till: Let no Senator hear the chest echo.
If we wobble, the Signoria may lend us a kind word. Only a word.
flush_till: The Arsenal is fitting a fleet. Our idle coin could be very patriotic.
Coin in the chest invites a forced loan. Better to offer one first.
high_leverage: The Senate is debating rules for the banchi. Let us not be the example.
Write less, or be ready to explain it to the Provveditori.
big_prince_exposure: Our loans to the Commune are our citizenship papers.
A bench the Republic owes cannot be allowed to fail. Probably.
bubble_city: The Council of Ten dislikes a bench that fails noisily. Lend quietly.
If it bursts, I want us on the right side of the Ten.
far_branches: Letters abroad pass through the Doge's eyes. Write accordingly.
A correspondent in Bruges is also an informant. Useful to the Signoria.
loss_turn: Losses can be described as service to the Republic.
Let me reach the Senator before the rumour does.
good_turn: Profits invite envy. A gift to the Arsenal would soothe it.
Good. Now the Signoria will want its share. Plan for that.
court_offer: One does not refuse the Serenissima. One negotiates the rate.
Lend, and our name sits in the Doge's ear for a generation.
new_tech: Is it permitted? I shall ask before we are fined for it.
The Senate likes any novelty that keeps the books clear for tax.
centre_moving: Venice is the centre of the world. Kindly lower your voice.
If the money moves, follow it with a Venetian passport.
quiet: A quiet turn is a fine time to dine with a Procurator.
Nothing to report to the Signoria. Excellent.

conscience.name: Fra Tomaso da Treviso
conscience.title: Confessore
conscience.bio: A Dominican who hears the partners' confessions weekly and their excuses daily, and prefers the confessions.

thin_till: Better a thin till than a fat sin.
Poverty is no shame. Failing the widows who trusted you is.
flush_till: Treasure that rusts accuses its owner. Alms cure rust.
Idle coin harms no one. Some of it might feed the poor of San Polo.
high_leverage: You promise ducats you do not have. That is a lie, neatly written.
Writing money from air smells of alchemy.
big_prince_exposure: Lending to the Commune is duty, and its interest a gift, not usury. Probably.
Princes sin too, but rarely confess it to their creditors.
bubble_city: Greed has gripped the city. I see it Sundays, in the empty poor box.
When every man wants the same pepper, the Devil is selling it.
far_branches: Far from home, a factor forgets his confessor.
A true bill of exchange is licit. A dry one is usury in a travelling cloak.
loss_turn: Perhaps God is reviewing your interest rates.
A loss is a sermon. Listen to it.
good_turn: Profit, yes. Was any of it usury? Tell me privately.
Leave a bequest for restitution in your will. In case.
court_offer: A loan to the Republic in war is near to charity. Charge modestly.
Serve the Doge, but do not charge him like a pawnbroker.
new_tech: Arab numerals? Count honestly in any numerals.
If it hides interest more cleverly, I shall find it anyway.
centre_moving: Wherever the money goes, the Church is there already.
Bruges also has confessors. Stricter ones.
quiet: A quiet turn. A good time for confession.
Remember: time belongs to God. You cannot sell it.

growth.name: Matteo di Ser Biagio Corsellini
growth.title: Direttore generale
growth.bio: Runs seven branches, three cardinals and one mistress, and keeps a separate ledger for each.

thin_till: The coin is in the branches. Draw a bill on Bruges.
Every great house runs thin. That is what branches are for.
flush_till: Florins idle while the Apostolic Camera needs funding? Shameful.
Open at Geneva. The fairs eat coin.
high_leverage: Partnership capital is small by design. The name carries the rest.
Our credit is our name, and our name is excellent.
big_prince_exposure: The Duke of Burgundy pays in time and in favours.
Lend to the King of England; the wool licences follow.
bubble_city: Bruges is booming. Raise the branch's limit.
Everyone lends in Bruges because Bruges is where the money is.
far_branches: Our London partner writes cheerfully. Cheer is profitable.
Each branch is its own partnership. If one fails, it fails alone.
loss_turn: A branch manager's error. Replace him and carry on.
Losses in London, profits in Rome. The whole is fine.
good_turn: The papal account carries us again. Bless the Curia.
Open another branch. Avignon looks lonely.
court_offer: A prince asking is a prince listening. Lend, and ask for the alum.
Kings make poor debtors and excellent customers.
new_tech: A holding of partnerships. Let us exploit it before others copy.
Printed exchange tables? Faster than a rival's abacus.
centre_moving: The centre is wherever our best branch is.
If Bruges rises, so does our Bruges partner's share.
quiet: Quiet? Write to every branch: find me a cardinal.
Idle partners are expensive partners.

prudence.name: Agnolo Fantoni
prudence.title: Ragioniere
prudence.bio: The first man in the house to own spectacles, which he uses chiefly to find errors in other men's arithmetic.

thin_till: A branch is only a promise in another city.
Recall the Bruges remittance before Bruges spends it.
flush_till: Let it sit. I have read the London ledgers.
A full chest has never ruined a house.
high_leverage: Ten thousand florins of capital, a hundred thousand of letters. Sleep well.
The name carries the rest, until the day it doesn't.
big_prince_exposure: Kings borrow for wars and repay with more wars.
The Burgundy loan now exceeds the Bruges branch. Count it.
bubble_city: When wool doubles, so does the foolishness.
The Bruges branch has lent to everyone in Bruges. That is the problem.
far_branches: London's accounts arrive in June describing a year that ended in March.
Branch managers lie by distance.
loss_turn: Audit the branch. In person, with a mule and a notary.
Fewer princes, more merchants.
good_turn: Repay the foreign lords' deposits. They are skittish.
Profit is pleasant. Reserves are wiser.
court_offer: Lend him wool, not florins.
The articles set a limit. Lend half of it.
new_tech: Spectacles are the only novelty I approve.
New schemes still need old arithmetic.
centre_moving: Moving the house costs more than missing the centre.
Let Bruges keep its glory and its bankruptcies.
quiet: Quiet is a ledger that balances.
I am checking the Geneva books. Again.

court.name: Messer Bernardo Tedaldini
court.title: Procuratore presso la Curia
court.bio: Young, charming and fluent in Latin flattery; has never met a cardinal he couldn't seat beside a creditor.

thin_till: Let no cardinal see us thin.
The Depositary of the Camera may lend a hand, discreetly.
flush_till: His Holiness wants a crusade financed. Piety with a rate.
Idle coin, if not offered, is often requested.
high_leverage: Leverage is invisible to princes, if we keep it so.
The Catasto officials count our florins. Keep the books tidy.
big_prince_exposure: A prince in our debt is a prince in our pocket. Or we in his.
The Pope's debts are holy. Their punctuality is not.
bubble_city: If Bruges collapses, the Duke will blame foreign bankers. Us.
Hot cities breed new laws against lenders.
far_branches: Our London man dines with the King. Encourage it.
Branches are embassies with ledgers.
loss_turn: A loss? Then a well-timed favour to the Duke.
Losses are better explained in person, over dinner.
good_turn: Profit! Now a chapel, a fresco and a grateful prior.
Show piety publicly. It calms both creditors and censors.
court_offer: Say yes elegantly. Negotiate the rate after.
Refuse a king and his heir remembers it too.
new_tech: The Curia dislikes surprises. Introduce it slowly.
If the prince's treasurer understands it, he will tax it.
centre_moving: Follow the court, not the coin.
Where the Pope goes, the money follows.
quiet: I am arranging a marriage with useful in-laws.
A quiet court is a court that is plotting.

conscience.name: Fra Silvestro Bocchetti
conscience.title: Confessore
conscience.bio: A Franciscan who preaches against avarice on Sunday and drafts the house's exchange contracts on Monday.

thin_till: Better poor and honest than bankrupt and damned.
A thin till is a humble till. Mind it stays honest.
flush_till: Give a tithe to the poor and a candle to San Francesco.
A chest full of florins is a sermon waiting to be preached.
high_leverage: Letters you cannot honour are false witness, sealed.
Pride goes before a fall, even in double entry.
big_prince_exposure: Lending to a prince for war is no sin, if the war is just.
Kings rarely pay their confessors either.
bubble_city: All Bruges runs after riches. Lent will come for Bruges.
When the city burns with gain, keep a bucket of penance near.
far_branches: Exchange between cities is licit. When the bill returns home unspent, it is not.
Dry exchange is usury in a travelling cloak.
loss_turn: God is tempering your margins.
Restitution, perhaps? It is never too early.
good_turn: Give one florin in ten. God keeps excellent books.
Gain is permitted. Gloating is not.
court_offer: A prince's loan is service, if the interest is a gift.
Lend to princes with prayer and a pledge.
new_tech: New contracts must still pass the canonists.
Clever instruments demand clever penance.
centre_moving: Bruges, Rome, London: your soul travels with you.
Moving the house does not move the sin.
quiet: Commission an altarpiece. For restitution, you understand.
A quiet turn. Confess the noisy ones.

growth.name: Gerolamo Vivaldini
growth.title: Fattore generale
growth.bio: A Genoese who can quote the Piacenza exchange rate in his sleep and has twice been woken to do so.

thin_till: We clear at the fair. Coin is for tavern keepers.
Roll the bills to the next fair and the till fills itself.
flush_till: Seville silver sitting idle? The King needs it in Flanders by Tuesday.
Idle coin at Antwerp is a crime against arbitrage.
high_leverage: An asiento is leverage wearing a crown.
Every Genoese house runs this way, and Genoa rules the fairs.
big_prince_exposure: The silver fleet comes every year. Every single year.
Philip is the richest prince alive. What could go wrong?
bubble_city: Antwerp is the Bourse of the world. Lend.
Pepper contracts double weekly in Antwerp. We should be in them.
far_branches: Our factors in Seville, Lyon and Antwerp write weekly. Distance is our profit.
Arbitrage lives in the weeks between cities.
loss_turn: The King's decree is a delay, not a default.
A rescheduling is merely a new asiento with better fees.
good_turn: The juros paid! Write another asiento.
Profit on the exchange. Double our stake at the next fair.
court_offer: Lend to the King; the silver will follow.
Name the rate and ask for export licences on silver.
new_tech: Bills negotiable by endorsement. Our paper travels without us.
The Antwerp Bourse trades all day. So must we.
centre_moving: The centre is the fair. The fair moves, and so do we.
If Amsterdam rises, we will own a corner of it.
quiet: Quiet means the King's treasurer is drafting a request.
Let us find a deposit from the Augsburg houses' rivals.

prudence.name: Margriet van Ooteghem
prudence.title: Boekhoudster
prudence.bio: Widowed by a merchant who believed in the fairs, she kept his books, paid his debts and believes in nothing.

thin_till: My late husband also said the fair would fill the till. Ask his creditors.
Keep enough coin for three days of withdrawals. Three.
flush_till: Coin in a chest has never yet gone bankrupt.
Keep it. Antwerp eats bankers in bad years.
high_leverage: Paper upon paper. It burns quickly.
I count the coin. The rest is wind from Genoa.
big_prince_exposure: The King of Spain decrees, and his creditors decay.
Philip owes half the Bourse. That is not security, it is company.
bubble_city: When the alleys smell of speculation, I sell.
Everyone buys pepper on credit. So I sell pepper.
far_branches: A letter from Seville is ten weeks stale when I read it.
Agents far away grow rich before we do.
loss_turn: Recount everything. Then recount it in silver.
Do not chase a loss with a king.
good_turn: Pay the depositors first. Celebrate second.
Profit I can count. Promises I cannot.
court_offer: Lend him a little. Princes repay a little.
Demand jewels in pledge, jewels I can hold.
new_tech: New paper is new trouble.
Endorsement only multiplies the people who might fail.
centre_moving: I stay with Antwerp till it burns.
Move, then. But the books travel with me.
quiet: I like quiet. Quiet I can audit.
Count the till before supper.

court.name: Don Diego de Arellano y Mesía
court.title: Agente en la Corte
court.bio: Lives in Valladolid on the house's money, writes beautiful letters, and is owed favours by three royal secretaries.

thin_till: The Contaduría need not know the till is thin.
A word from the King's secretary steadies depositors wonderfully.
flush_till: His Majesty notices idle silver. Offer it before he asks.
Idle coin in Flanders is coin the rebels may seize.
high_leverage: At court they call it confidence. Let us not correct them.
Leverage is invisible as long as His Majesty smiles.
big_prince_exposure: To be owed by Spain is to be a grandee of credit.
If the King suspends payments, I will negotiate the settlement myself.
bubble_city: The Regent of the Netherlands dislikes failures on the Bourse.
Speculation brings edicts. I hear them drafting one now.
far_branches: Our factor in Seville must charm the Casa de Contratación.
Distance from court is distance from favour.
loss_turn: The Council of Finance may compensate us in juros.
Ask for a monopoly to repair the loss.
good_turn: Profits make the King's accountants curious.
Send a gift to the King. He will remember it at the next default.
court_offer: One does not refuse His Catholic Majesty.
Accept, and fix the silver licences into the contract.
new_tech: If it serves the Crown's wars, the court will approve.
Innovation is welcome until the Inquisition reads it.
centre_moving: The court is the centre. Everything else is commerce.
Wherever the King's silver lands, we stand.
quiet: A quiet court is planning a war.
I am buying our senior partner a title. Modestly priced.

conscience.name: Fray Melchor de Arteaga
conscience.title: Confesor y teólogo
conscience.bio: A Salamanca-trained Dominican who can justify any exchange contract in Latin, and condemn it in Castilian.

thin_till: A thin till endangers widows' deposits. That is sin, not daring.
Deposits are a trust before they are a resource.
flush_till: Coin held idle harms none. Lent at usury, it harms many.
Alms are a better investment than the Bourse.
high_leverage: Your paper outruns your coin. The Salamanca masters would frown.
Risk taken with others' money does not earn lucrum cessans.
big_prince_exposure: A loan for just war is licit. Is this war just?
Interest from the Crown is compensation for damnum emergens. Probably.
bubble_city: The just price is the common estimation. Antwerp has lost its common sense.
Speculation is not trade. Recall Saint Thomas.
far_branches: Real exchange between places is licit. Bills that go nowhere are dry exchange.
Confirm that the bills truly travel.
loss_turn: Losses are no sin. Lying about them is.
Do penance by honest accounts.
good_turn: Profit from true exchange is licit. From fictitious bills, damnable.
Endow a chapel. It clears the conscience.
court_offer: The King's war becomes your sin if it is unjust.
Lend, but do not charge for time itself.
new_tech: Each new paper needs new casuistry. I am ready.
Endorsement is licit. Rolling bills to nowhere is not.
centre_moving: The Calvinists lend freely in the north. Do not follow them.
Moving north moves you out of Rome's sight, not God's.
quiet: Examine your contracts, one by one.
A quiet turn for confession.

growth.name: Jacob Ruysdonck
growth.title: Koopman-bankier
growth.bio: Owns VOC shares, two herring busses and one regrettable tulip bulb, and has never once read a prospectus.

thin_till: Our money is in the Wisselbank. Same as coin, only safer.
Draw on Hamburg. We settle in a fortnight.
flush_till: VOC shares, sir, or bulbs if you have the stomach.
Idle guilders vex me. Lend to the Baltic grain men.
high_leverage: Every merchant on the Dam borrows. Amsterdam is leverage.
Bank money is better than coin, so we may stretch it.
big_prince_exposure: The States always pay; they are merchants themselves.
King Charles is good for it. Ask any London goldsmith.
bubble_city: Bulbs rise weekly. We must lend or look foolish.
Speculation is merely commerce with ambition.
far_branches: Our man in Batavia writes once a year, profitably.
Ships carry letters and profits together.
loss_turn: Bad wind. Good winds follow.
Sell short on the Beurs and recover by Friday.
good_turn: Profits at the Beurs! More ships.
We should open a counting house in London.
court_offer: The Stadtholder needs money. He pays in favours.
Lend to the English Crown. The goldsmiths do.
new_tech: Bank money! Faster than coin and cleaner.
Joint stock is the future. Buy.
centre_moving: London is rising. Send a partner.
If the centre moves, move faster than it.
quiet: Quiet? The Beurs is never quiet.
Find me a voyage.

prudence.name: Cornelis Swaenswijck
prudence.title: Kassier
prudence.bio: Has kept the house's coin for forty years in a chest with three locks, carrying two keys and suspecting the third.

thin_till: A till this thin invites a run.
Keep guilders in the chest against the bad morning.
flush_till: Better guilders in the chest than bulbs in the ground.
I sleep on a heavy chest.
high_leverage: Amsterdam is leverage. Amsterdam also has a paupers' graveyard.
Paper is fine until everyone wants coin.
big_prince_exposure: Kings close their exchequers. Mark me.
Charles of England will stop payment one day.
bubble_city: A bulb is an onion with ambition.
When the chimney sweep buys shares, sell yours.
far_branches: Batavia is a year away. Fraud is faster.
Distance turns honest clerks into nabobs.
loss_turn: Retrench. Sell what you do not understand.
Write it plain: we lost.
good_turn: Put half of it into Wisselbank money.
Pay down debt while the sun shines.
court_offer: Lend to the States, not to kings.
The English Crown has a short memory for debts.
new_tech: The Wisselbank is sound because it does not lend. Remember that.
New is not wrong. New is untested.
centre_moving: London is a nest of goldsmiths and debtors.
Let them move. Amsterdam coin stays honest.
quiet: Quiet days, sound books.
I am counting the till.

court.name: Adriaen van Coeverden
court.title: Agent bij de Staten-Generaal
court.bio: The son of a burgomaster's cousin, he believes every problem in Amsterdam can be solved over oysters with the right magistrate.

thin_till: The Wisselbank commissioners would be distressed. Let us not distress them.
The burgomasters prefer solvent bankers.
flush_till: The States need war money against France.
Patriotic loans buy tolerance.
high_leverage: The magistrates are drafting rules on credit. Tread softly.
Leverage in Amsterdam is a matter of politics.
big_prince_exposure: The States pay; they are merchants like us.
English kings come and go. Their debts stay.
bubble_city: The magistrates will ban the bulb trade soon.
Speculation leads to ordinances.
far_branches: The VOC directors are good friends to have.
Distance is managed through marriage.
loss_turn: The burgomasters can be sympathetic.
A loss is a fine reason to petition for a privilege.
good_turn: A donation to the orphanage. Publicly.
Profit noticed is profit taxed.
court_offer: The Stadtholder asks, the States agree, we lend.
A new king in London seeks Dutch bankers. Go.
new_tech: The new Bank in London borrows our methods. Watch it.
Innovation needs a charter first.
centre_moving: Follow the Stadtholder to London.
Where the court goes, credit goes.
quiet: I am dining with a burgomaster.
Quiet. Good for petitions.

conscience.name: Dominee Gerrit Abbema
conscience.title: Predikant
conscience.bio: A Reformed minister who permits interest on Calvin's authority and forbids enjoyment of it on his own.

thin_till: Better a thin till than robbed depositors.
A steward must render account.
flush_till: Wealth is a trust from God. Give.
Do not bury your talent. But do not gamble it either.
high_leverage: Debt is a chain. Calvin permits interest, not folly.
Reckless credit shames the congregation.
big_prince_exposure: Popish kings repay in promises.
Lend to Protestant princes, prudently.
bubble_city: Bulbs are vanity. Ecclesiastes said so.
When greed blooms, pray.
far_branches: In the Indies our men forget God.
Send admonitions with the orders.
loss_turn: Providence humbles.
A loss is a summons to repentance.
good_turn: Profit is blessing. Remember the poor box.
Sober gain is no sin.
court_offer: Render unto Caesar, at moderate interest.
Lend if the cause is godly.
new_tech: Honest bank money is a blessing.
Novelty tempts. Pray first.
centre_moving: London is full of bishops and luxury.
God is not confined to Amsterdam.
quiet: Read the Psalms between the ledgers.
Quiet. Good for sobriety.

growth.name: Josiah Pennefather Hale
growth.title: Senior Partner
growth.bio: Has founded two banks, one turnpike trust and a canal that runs nowhere, and is cheerful about all four.

thin_till: We'll draw on our London agent. That's what he's for.
Our notes circulate, sir. Gold is old-fashioned.
flush_till: Canal shares, sir. Turnpikes. Anything with a toll.
Idle guineas! Discount more bills.
high_leverage: Our notes are as good as gold, so long as no one asks.
Every country bank issues. We issue better.
big_prince_exposure: Consols are the safest thing in England.
The Government always pays. It has the Navy.
bubble_city: South Sea stock is rising. Buy.
Manchester is booming. Open a branch.
far_branches: Our Bristol correspondent is perfectly reliable.
An agency in Calcutta? Letters take months; so do profits.
loss_turn: A bad harvest. Next year will mend it.
One poor quarter. Discount more.
good_turn: Splendid. Open a branch in Leeds.
Profit! Issue more notes.
court_offer: The Treasury needs a war loan. Patriotism at five per cent.
Lend to the Government. They print the bonds.
new_tech: The cheque! Quicker than notes.
Railway shares, sir. They never lose.
centre_moving: London is the City, sir. Open there.
Our notes clear through Lombard Street anyway.
quiet: Quiet? Let's buy a mill.
Advertise for depositors.

prudence.name: Mrs Hester Clewlow
prudence.title: Partner
prudence.bio: Inherited her husband's share and his ledgers; kept the share, corrected the ledgers, and has outlived two runs.

thin_till: Mr Clewlow kept a third in gold. He also died solvent.
Recall the London balance at once.
flush_till: Gold in the vault never ran on anyone.
Keep it. The panic of 'ninety-three is not forgotten in this town.
high_leverage: Our notes are promises. Promises run.
Fewer notes, gentlemen.
big_prince_exposure: Consols fall in war. Hold fewer.
The Government suspends gold payments when it suits.
bubble_city: When the parson buys South Sea, sell.
Railway mania is still mania.
far_branches: Branches far off mean clerks far off.
A cashier in Bristol can embezzle for a year undetected.
loss_turn: Retrench. Call in the weaker loans.
Write to the London agent today.
good_turn: Add it to the reserve.
Pay off the London overdraft.
court_offer: Lend to the Treasury, never to dukes.
Ministers make poor guarantors.
new_tech: The cheque merely makes fraud quicker.
Railways need capital, not our depositors' savings.
centre_moving: London takes our money and our nerve.
Stay country. We know our borrowers.
quiet: Quiet is profitable.
Balance the books, then the books again.

court.name: Sir Ambrose Kettlewood
court.title: Parliamentary Agent
court.bio: Sits for a borough with eleven voters, nine of whom bank with the house; considers this public service.

thin_till: The Bank of England discounts for its friends.
Keep friends in Threadneedle Street.
flush_till: The Chancellor seeks subscribers.
Idle money offends the Treasury.
high_leverage: Parliament is debating note issue. Be discreet.
Peel's men are counting country notes.
big_prince_exposure: Holding Consols makes us patriots.
A Government that owes us must support us.
bubble_city: Parliament passes Bubble Acts after bubbles.
A collapse will bring legislation, and inquiries.
far_branches: See that the county members are customers.
Branches bring votes.
loss_turn: Perhaps a Treasury remittance contract.
I shall speak with the Bank.
good_turn: Subscribe to the war loan.
Profit noticed by Parliament is profit taxed.
court_offer: Lend to the Crown. Knighthoods follow.
Accept, and ask for the Army remittance business.
new_tech: Parliament likes cheques; they are not notes.
Railway bills pass with the right friends.
centre_moving: London is where Parliament sits.
Be in the City or be forgotten.
quiet: I am dining with an under-secretary.
Quiet. Prepare petitions.

conscience.name: Ezra Thistlewaite
conscience.title: Elder and Counsel
conscience.bio: A Quaker elder who holds that a bank which fails its depositors fails God, and that this is worse than failing Parliament.

thin_till: Plain dealing: keep coin enough to pay all.
A Friend never fails his creditors.
flush_till: Surplus may relieve the poor of the parish.
Idle wealth is at least wealth spared from vanity.
high_leverage: To promise more than thou hast is untruth.
The Meeting disowns members who fail.
big_prince_exposure: Lending for war troubles me.
War loans buy cannon. Friends abstain.
bubble_city: South Sea? I would not touch it.
Vanity, in shares.
far_branches: Bills from the slave trade pass through Bristol. Refuse them.
Know whom thy correspondents serve.
loss_turn: Losses must be borne truthfully.
Make good thy creditors first.
good_turn: Profit is honest when the measure is honest.
Give to the abolition fund.
court_offer: The Crown wants guns. I counsel no.
The law allows five per cent. Charge no more, and lend for roads.
new_tech: The cheque is honest if honoured.
Railways join distant Meetings. Good.
centre_moving: Lombard Street has many Friends.
Move only if the Meeting there will receive thee.
quiet: Silence is a good counsellor.
Wait in the Light.

growth.name: Augustus Merriman-Lowe
growth.title: Senior Partner
growth.bio: Has floated loans for four republics and two emperors, and regards the occasional default as character-building for others.

thin_till: The Bank lends freely in a panic. Everyone knows the rule.
We'll rediscount at Threadneedle Street. Stop fretting.
flush_till: Argentine railways, five per cent guaranteed.
Idle money in the City is an insult to the City.
high_leverage: Every accepting house runs lean.
Leverage is the price of a seat in Lombard Street.
big_prince_exposure: Argentina will pay; it has beef.
The Russian loan is oversubscribed twice.
bubble_city: Buenos Aires is the new Chicago.
Wall Street is roaring. Let us roar with it.
far_branches: Our Shanghai agency is a gold mine.
The cable makes the Empire one market.
loss_turn: One bad bill. The Bank will discount the rest.
Losses happen. Bigger deals follow.
good_turn: Splendid. Another foreign loan.
Profit! Take a bigger floor on the Exchange.
court_offer: A government loan! Flotation fees of three per cent.
Lend, and the Foreign Office smiles.
new_tech: The telephone, sir. Faster than any clerk.
Cable to New York; arbitrage by noon.
centre_moving: New York is a provincial town with ambitions.
If New York rises, open there. Quietly.
quiet: Quiet? Let's float something.
Find me a foreign railway.

prudence.name: Mr Silas Pettigrew
prudence.title: Chief Accountant
prudence.bio: Bald since Overend Gurney and blames it; keeps a framed copy of the 1866 Bank Rate above his desk.

thin_till: Remember Overend Gurney. Everyone in this building should.
Keep cash at the Bank, and more than you think.
flush_till: Cash has never failed a bank.
Reserves are dull. Dull survives.
high_leverage: Acceptances are liabilities, gentlemen, whatever the partners say.
Leverage is a rope. Mind your neck.
big_prince_exposure: Argentina has defaulted before. It will again.
Foreign governments enjoy defaulting.
bubble_city: When the office boy buys shares, sell.
Wall Street will crash, and New York will drag us with it.
far_branches: The Shanghai agent gambles with our name.
The cable shows prices, not fraud.
loss_turn: Write down the bad bills now.
Call in loans before the rumour.
good_turn: Add it to the reserve fund.
Pay down acceptances.
court_offer: Take the fees. Do not keep the bonds.
Governments promise; creditors wait.
new_tech: The typewriter is noisy and the clerks are slower.
Machines cannot judge a borrower's character.
centre_moving: Keep sterling. Let dollars wander.
London has survived worse.
quiet: A quiet turn is my favourite.
Balance the reserve.

court.name: Captain Rupert Daunsey
court.title: Liaison to Threadneedle Street
court.bio: A Guards officer who resigned for the City; knows the Governor's moods, his club and the name of his dog.

thin_till: The Governor's eyebrows are our regulation.
A word at the Discount Office, before anyone else's word.
flush_till: The Bank likes reserves. Tell them.
The Treasury needs a war loan.
high_leverage: The Governor will raise an eyebrow. One is enough.
Keep it quiet, and keep it off the club gossip.
big_prince_exposure: The Foreign Office supports this loan.
Patriotic lending. Whitehall will remember.
bubble_city: The Bank dislikes speculation. Expect Bank Rate to rise.
If it ends badly, the Governor asks who lent most.
far_branches: The Colonial Office approves of our agencies.
An office in Cairo is useful. To several people.
loss_turn: The Bank can organise a lifeboat. For friends.
Let me discuss it with the Governor.
good_turn: Subscribe to the war loan.
Dinner at the Mansion House, then.
court_offer: A foreign loan with Whitehall behind it. Safe as houses.
His Majesty's Government will appreciate it.
new_tech: The Bank uses the telephone now. So may we.
New methods should be shown to the Governor first.
centre_moving: Sterling is the world's money.
New York? A passing fancy.
quiet: Quiet. Good for lunch at the club.
I'll have a chat with the Deputy Governor.

conscience.name: Mr Lionel Grieve
conscience.title: Company Solicitor
conscience.bio: Reads every prospectus twice and every partner's letter three times; the partners call him 'the Vicar' behind his back.

thin_till: Directors who trade while insolvent may answer personally.
Do not take deposits you know you cannot repay.
flush_till: Idle cash breaks no law.
Excess cash is legally safe.
high_leverage: Limited liability is limited.
Directors may be prosecuted.
big_prince_exposure: Sovereign immunity: you cannot sue a king.
Bondholders' committees are slow and sad.
bubble_city: Puffed prospectuses become fraud claims.
Check the prospectus; I shall.
far_branches: Foreign law differs, and so do foreign juries.
Opium bills? Not in this house, whatever is legal.
loss_turn: Disclose it to the shareholders.
Truthful accounts, gentlemen.
good_turn: Pay a dividend, not a bonus.
Remember the shareholders.
court_offer: Read the bond covenant before signing.
Is the treaty sound? Check it.
new_tech: The telephone leaves no record. Write it down after.
Typed contracts still need signatures.
centre_moving: New York law is unfamiliar.
Stay under English law.
quiet: I am reading the articles of association.
Reviewing the minute book.

growth.name: Trent Halvorsen
growth.title: Head of Global Markets
growth.bio: Ran the rates desk at thirty-one; believes risk models are suggestions and bonuses are human rights.

thin_till: Liquidity's a funding-desk problem. Roll it in repo overnight like grown-ups.
The Fed has a window for a reason. Stop panicking.
flush_till: Cash on the balance sheet is negative carry. Deploy it or buy back stock.
We're sitting on a fortress of nothing. Put it to work.
high_leverage: Thirty-to-one is industry standard. Ask anyone on the Street.
Leverage is just ROE that hasn't been explained to Risk yet.
big_prince_exposure: Sovereigns in the euro don't default. That's the whole point of the euro.
Zero risk weight, juicy spread. Basel practically begs us.
bubble_city: House prices haven't fallen nationally since the Depression. Write the paper.
Everyone's lending there because it works. Want market share or a lecture?
far_branches: Singapore trades while London sleeps. That's not distance, it's coverage.
Book it offshore. The model doesn't care where the server is.
loss_turn: Six-sigma event. Won't happen again for ten thousand years.
One bad quarter. Don't let Risk cut my limits over noise.
good_turn: Record quarter. Bonus pool, then a bigger desk.
Size works. Double the book before competitors notice.
court_offer: Underwriting fees plus repo-eligible collateral. What's not to love?
Primary dealer status is franchise. Lend to the Treasury.
new_tech: AI execution, tokenized deposits. Adopt now or become a case study.
Electronic trading means volume. Volume means us.
centre_moving: Flow's moved. Put the desk where the flow is, tomorrow.
Frankfurt, Dublin, Singapore. I'll go wherever basis points live.
quiet: Low vol? Sell volatility. Free money.
Quiet markets are when you build positions.

prudence.name: Dr Meera Vasudevan
prudence.title: Chief Risk Officer
prudence.bio: A former physicist who models tail risk for a living and has stopped being invited to the markets Christmas party.

thin_till: Our LCR is under a hundred. Social media can empty a bank in a day now.
Liquidity is a funding-desk problem until it's everyone's problem.
flush_till: That buffer is HQLA, not idle cash. It's why we exist on Monday.
Excess liquidity is insurance. Nobody complains about insurance during the fire.
high_leverage: The leverage ratio ignores your models. So will the market.
Thirty-to-one means a three per cent fall ends us.
big_prince_exposure: Zero risk weight is a regulatory fiction, not a credit view.
One sovereign, huge concentration. It's going in the stress scenario.
bubble_city: Everyone's lending there. That's the risk, not the reassurance.
Run the severely adverse scenario on that book. I'll wait.
far_branches: Who checks the Singapore desk's marks at three in the morning?
Remote booking entities are where rogue traders hide.
loss_turn: Six-sigma events happen every few years. The model is wrong.
Cut limits, raise capital, then argue.
good_turn: Retain it. CET1 is the only friend that stays.
Good quarter. Now ask what we got lucky on.
court_offer: Long sovereign duration reprices fast. Ask a regional bank.
Lend if the rate risk is hedged. Is it hedged?
new_tech: New tech is new operational risk. Where's model validation?
Tokenized deposits run faster than the paper kind.
centre_moving: Moving entities moves risk, not just people.
Relocation is a capital event. Price it.
quiet: Quiet is when you build buffers.
Stress test. Again.

court.name: Colette Ashworth-Baptiste
court.title: Head of Regulatory Affairs
court.bio: Ex-central banker who crossed to the private side and now briefs her former colleagues, who pretend not to remember her.

thin_till: The supervisor will call before the market does. Better they hear it from us.
The discount window carries stigma. Let's not need it.
flush_till: Supervisors love buffers. Let me tell them how big ours is.
Spare capital buys goodwill at the next stress test.
high_leverage: We're near the next G-SIB surcharge bucket. One step costs fifty basis points.
The Fed reads leverage ratios before breakfast.
big_prince_exposure: Home treasuries are politically protected. Foreign ones are not.
The supervisor will ask about concentration. I'll need a story.
bubble_city: Expect a countercyclical buffer and loan-to-value caps.
If it bursts there'll be hearings. Let's not be the witness.
far_branches: Every jurisdiction wants a ring-fenced subsidiary now.
Resolution planners hate complexity. Our living will runs nine hundred pages.
loss_turn: I'll brief the supervisor this afternoon. No surprises.
Losses invite the enforcement team. Let's be helpful.
good_turn: Don't announce buybacks before the stress test result.
Regulators notice record bonuses. So do legislators.
court_offer: Supporting the sovereign auction keeps the Treasury on side.
Primary dealer status is a seat at their table.
new_tech: The regulators want it in a sandbox first.
Crypto? The SEC will have opinions.
centre_moving: Passporting is gone. We need a licence there.
Wherever we go, supervision follows.
quiet: I'm lunching with the Fed liaison.
Good time to comment on the Basel III endgame drafts.

conscience.name: Samuel Achterberg
conscience.title: Chief Compliance Officer
conscience.bio: Has read every trader chat since 2008 and no longer believes in humanity, only in archived messages.

thin_till: Don't let liquidity pressure become disclosure pressure.
Misleading depositors is fraud, even in a crisis.
flush_till: Idle cash is quiet. Quiet is legal.
Better idle than laundered.
high_leverage: Leverage tempts mismarking. I've read those emails before.
No off-balance-sheet vehicles to hide it. Not again.
big_prince_exposure: Some sovereigns come with sanctions attached. Check the list.
Politically exposed persons behind that wealth fund. Enhanced due diligence.
bubble_city: Hot lending means liar loans. Pull the files.
Today's mis-selling is a fine in five years.
far_branches: Offshore entities are where AML fails.
Know your customer in every country, not just the home one.
loss_turn: Losses tempt cover-ups. Don't.
Report it fully. The cover-up is always the bigger fine.
good_turn: Profitable? Check where it came from.
Record quarter. I'll be reading the chats.
court_offer: Sanctions screening first, then the term sheet.
Lending to kleptocracies makes headlines.
new_tech: Crypto rails are laundering highways.
AI models must be explainable to supervisors.
centre_moving: New jurisdiction, new rules. Train the staff.
Different law, same ethics.
quiet: Training season.
Checking the messaging app archives.

rivals.name: the Peruzzi

fates.text: Bankrupt with Edward III owing it 600,000 florins. The second company of Florence is gone.

rivals.text: The second of Florence's super-companies: wool, grain, the Curia's money, and the King of England's debts.

rivals.name: the Bardi

fates.text: 900,000 florins owed by Edward III. The largest bank in Europe stops, and the Acciaiuoli with it.

rivals.text: The largest bank in Europe, with branches from London to Cyprus. Lent Edward III the wool customs and more.
rivals.source: Hunt (1994); Russell, 'The societies of the Bardi and the Peruzzi'

rivals.name: the Medici

fates.text: The Bruges branch is insolvent on Charles the Bold's debts; London follows. The bank contracts to Florence, Rome and Lyon.
Charles VIII marches into Florence, Piero flees, the palace is sacked and the bank dissolved.

rivals.text: Giovanni di Bicci's house: one parent, many partnerships, the Curia's account, and for seventy years a rule against lending to princes.
rivals.source: de Roover, The Rise and Decline of the Medici Bank (1963)

rivals.name: the Lippomano

fates.text: Stops in May 1499, the day before the crowd runs on Pisani. The family never recovers its standing.

rivals.text: A Rialto bench that grew on the Cappello brothers' capital until they retired and left Lippomano to run it.
rivals.source: Mueller, The Venetian Money Market; Sanudo

rivals.name: the Pisani–Tiepolo

fates.text: Propped by the Mint in 1576, the last private bank on the Rialto succumbs to a run. Three years later Venice founds a public bank instead.

rivals.text: Survived the run of 1499 when the crowd came for its coin and found it. By 1570 the only private bank left in Venice.

rivals.name: the Fuggers

fates.text: Spain's bankruptcy converts the Fuggers' asientos into juros worth a fraction. The Habsburgs' bankers for forty years will never be so again.
The last Fugger counting-house closes. The family keeps its titles and its land.

rivals.text: Jakob the Rich: Tyrolean silver, Hungarian copper, the Emperor's election bought for 850,000 florins. The richest house in Europe.
rivals.source: Ehrenberg, Capital and Finance in the Age of the Renaissance; Steinmetz, The Richest Man Who Ever Lived

rivals.name: the Welsers

fates.text: Matthäus Welser's bankruptcy. Venezuela, lent to the Emperor, did not pay.

rivals.text: The Fuggers' Augsburg rivals; held Venezuela as a fief from Charles V and lost money on it.

rivals.name: the Genoese

fates.text: Philip IV's stop of 1627 and the Portuguese New Christians who replace them. The Genoese keep their fairs and lose the crown.
The last asientos are gone; Genoa's capital goes into other people's bonds.

rivals.text: Spinola, Centurione, Grimaldi: the consortium that took the Spanish crown's debt from the Fuggers and ran the fairs at Piacenza.

rivals.name: Backwell and Vyner

fates.text: The Stop of the Exchequer. Backwell owed £295,000 by the Crown; Vyner £416,000. Both are ruined, and their depositors with them.

rivals.text: The greatest goldsmith-bankers of Lombard Street, lending the Crown next year's revenue against orders on the Exchequer.

rivals.name: Hoare's
rivals.text: At the sign of the Golden Bottle on Fleet Street. Still owned by the family. Never failed, never grew much, never had to.

rivals.name: the Casa di San Giorgio

fates.text: Napoleon annexes the Ligurian Republic and dissolves the Casa. Four centuries as the Republic's creditor, tax-farmer and bank end with a decree.

rivals.text: The Republic of Genoa's creditors, organised as a company that collected its taxes, governed Corsica, and kept a bank of deposit.
rivals.source: Fratianni, 'Government Debt, Reputation and Creditors' Protections: The Tale of San Giorgio' (2006)

rivals.name: Berenberg
rivals.text: Founded by Flemish Protestants fleeing Antwerp. Never failed, never sold; the oldest bank of its kind still trading.

rivals.name: Palmer & Co.

fates.text: John Palmer, 'the prince of merchants', stops in January 1830 with debts of some £5 million, lent to indigo planters who could not pay. The other agency houses follow by 1834.

rivals.text: The greatest of Calcutta's agency houses: deposits from the Company's servants, loans to indigo and to Indian princes.
rivals.source: Webster, The Twilight of the East India Company (2009)

rivals.name: Jardine Matheson
rivals.text: Founded in Canton on opium and tea; moved to Hong Kong in 1842 and never looked back. A taipan's house, not a bank, but everyone's banker in the treaty ports.
rivals.source: Keswick (ed.), The Thistle and the Jade (1982)

rivals.name: Hope & Co.

fates.text: After the French occupation the house passes to its London correspondent. Baring Brothers own the name.

rivals.text: Amsterdam's great house: Russian, Swedish, Portuguese loans, and half of Louisiana with Barings.
rivals.source: Buist, At Spes Non Fracta: Hope & Co 1770–1815

rivals.name: Barings

fates.text: £21 million of Argentine paper and insolvent. The Governor's guarantee fund, raised from every house in the City in a weekend, lets it be liquidated and refounded as a limited company.
Nick Leeson's futures positions in Singapore, hidden in account 88888: £827 million. Sold to ING for £1.

rivals.text: Francis Baring's house: trade, then acceptance, then sovereign loans. 'The sixth great power.'

rivals.name: N M Rothschild
rivals.text: Nathan Mayer's house: the Waterloo bullion, the 1818 French loans, every sovereign issue of the century. Still private.

rivals.name: Overend, Gurney & Co.

fates.text: Refused by the Bank as insolvent on 9 May; suspends at 3.30 on the 10th. Black Friday, and the lender of last resort born the same afternoon.

rivals.text: The corner house: the greatest discount house in the world, until it went into shipping and railways with money it had borrowed at call.
rivals.source: Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin 2016 Q4

rivals.name: the City of Glasgow Bank

fates.text: £6 million of losses hidden by false accounts. Unlimited: 1,819 shareholders called for £2,750 a share, 1,565 of them ruined.

rivals.text: 133 branches and a board that lent to itself and to Australian sheep.

rivals.name: the Midland Bank

fates.text: Weakened by Crocker in California, bought by HSBC. The largest bank in the world in 1934; a brand retired in 1999.

rivals.text: Birmingham, then Threadneedle Street; by 1934 the largest bank in the world by deposits. The clearers' clearer.
rivals.source: Holmes & Green, Midland: 150 Years of Banking Business

rivals.name: J.P. Morgan
rivals.text: Drexel, Morgan & Co.: stopped the panic of 1907 from a library on Madison Avenue. Split by Glass–Steagall; reunited by 1999.

rivals.name: the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank
rivals.text: Founded for the China trade; bought Midland in 1992 and moved its seat to London for it. A G-SIB in bucket 2 or 3 every year since the list began.
rivals.source: King, The History of the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation

rivals.name: S.G. Warburg

fates.text: After a failed merger with Morgan Stanley, bought by Swiss Bank Corporation. The last independent London investment bank of the first rank.

rivals.text: Siegmund Warburg's house: the first Eurobond (Autostrade, 1963), the hostile takeover, Big Bang's most ambitious buyer.

rivals.name: BCCI

fates.text: Closed by the Bank of England on 5 July 1991 with $10 billion missing. Supervised in Luxembourg, booked in the Caymans, run from London.

rivals.text: The Bank of Credit and Commerce International: a million depositors in seventy countries and no consolidated supervisor.

rivals.name: Northern Rock

fates.text: Funded three-quarters in the wholesale market, which closes in August. The first run on a British bank in 140 years, in September; nationalised in February.

rivals.text: A Newcastle building society that became a mortgage bank with Granite, its securitisation vehicle, and 'Together' loans at 125% of value.
rivals.source: Treasury Committee, The Run on the Rock (2008)

rivals.name: Lehman Brothers

fates.text: 15 September 2008. The largest bankruptcy in history; the interbank market closes behind it.

rivals.text: Cotton brokers in Montgomery, Alabama; investment bankers on Wall Street; $600 billion of balance sheet at 31 times leverage.

geo.land_source: Natural Earth 1:50m land, public domain, via world-atlas 2.0.2 (ISC)
